issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims rigorous error bounds for both proposed approaches, but the formal error bounds apply only to an existence construction from the epsilon-rank theorem or to a CUR decomposition whose index sets have maximal volume. The adaptive algorithms select fixed symmetric blocks around zero and are not shown to satisfy the maximal-volume hypothesis or to achieve the stated bounds.

failure_location.quote: Theoretical error bounds are derived for both approaches, ensuring rigorous control over approximation quality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove that the adaptive algorithms produce index sets meeting the hypotheses of the error bounds or restrict the guarantee to the maximal-volume CUR construction and remove the claim for the adaptive algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central claim that the adaptive algorithms come with rigorous approximation guarantees is unsupported.
issues.title: Prose overclaims rigorous error bounds for adaptive algorithms
issues.why_classification: The advertised rigorous control for the main adaptive methods is a central guarantee; supporting it requires new proofs or a major withdrawal of the claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof combines with Theorem general-theorem-main, which bounds the truncation error by C min{I1,I2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha. Since max{I1,I2} >= min{I1,I2}, max^{-alpha} <= min^{-alpha}; the stated bound with max is stronger and does not follow. In anisotropic cases the smaller truncation order governs the error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace max{I1,I2} by min{I1,I2} in the theorem and corollary, accepting the weaker valid bound.
issues.overall_effect: The main approximation error bound is overstated for anisotropic truncation orders; the corollary inherits the same false rate.
issues.title: Error bound uses max instead of min truncation order
issues.why_classification: The repair is local but changes the rate in anisotropic regimes, so it is more than a pure typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The Fourier basis is orthonormal, so the squared L2 norm of the difference equals the sum of squared coefficient differences, i.e., the Frobenius norm of A-EF*. The Frobenius norm is at least the maximum-entry norm, not at most it. Thus the displayed inequality is false. Theorem epsilonrank-main only gives a maximum-entry bound, so it cannot control the L2 error as claimed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the max-norm control by a genuine Frobenius-norm low-rank approximation bound or account for the dimension factor, which changes the advertised rate.
issues.overall_effect: The core L2 error bounds in Theorem general-approximation-main and Corollary cor:added-1 are invalid; the rank-R construction does not necessarily give L2 error epsilon||A||_2.
issues.title: L2 error bounded by maximum-entry error
issues.why_classification: The main theoretical guarantee is invalid; a correct proof would require a different norm-conversion argument or a new low-rank approximation theorem, a major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The input declares K as the maximum number of iterations, but the loop continues while either tol>tau or k<=K. It therefore runs at least K+1 iterations when tol<=tau and can run beyond K when tol>tau. The intended guard should use 'and' (or k<K).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the condition to 'tol>tau and k<=K' (or an equivalent conjunction with the correct iteration bound).
issues.overall_effect: Algorithms alg1, alg2, and alg1:app may not terminate at the stated maximum iteration count and can run indefinitely if the tolerance is never met.
issues.title: Loop condition does not enforce maximum iterations
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction restores the stated iteration bound without changing the mathematical method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d)

issues.failure_explanation: The prose requires both C and R to satisfy the relative singular-value condition (max of the two squared ratios < tau^2). The algorithm sets tol to the minimum of the two ratios and stops when tol<=tau, i.e., when at least one of C or R satisfies the condition. It can therefore stop while the other matrix is still ill-conditioned.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the maximum of the two ratios in the tolerance computation, or change the prose condition to match the min-based stopping rule.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg1 can terminate prematurely and return C,R that do not meet the stated tolerance condition.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 termination uses min instead of max
issues.why_classification: A local change to the tolerance definition fixes the mismatch.

issues.failure_explanation: The pseudocode never updates T_n after adding the new blocks. Consequently, T_n remains {0} in later iterations, so G_{1k} and G_{2k} are computed with the old T_n and have dimensions incompatible with the growing block matrix G. The algorithm is not well-defined for more than one iteration. The same omission occurs in Algorithm alg1:app.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing update T_n = T_n union T_n' inside the loop.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg2 and the appendix modification cannot proceed as written beyond the first iteration.
issues.title: Algorithm 2 omits the update of T_n
issues.why_classification: The prose already contains the intended update; adding the omitted line is a local repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \STATE Compute $\mathbf{C}$ according to (\ref{t-lasso:method-one:sub1-main}) with $\mathbb{T}_2$, and $\mathbf{R}$ according to (\ref{t-lasso:method-one:sub2-main}) with $\mathbb{T}_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: To form C and R, the algorithm must compute all entries in their union, whose size is (2I1+1)S2 + S1(2I2+1) - S1S2. The diagonal blocks of G are a subset of this union, so the total number of distinct integrals cannot be less than this union. The claimed formula subtracts an additional S1S2 - Kb1b2, corresponding to cross entries of G that are still needed for C and R. For example, with I1=I2=1, S1=S2=3, K=b1=b2=1, the formula gives 1 integral, but C and R already require 9 distinct entries. Thus the claim that alg1:app needs fewer integrals is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the integral count; the correct count is at least the union size (2I1+1)S2 + S1(2I2+1) - S1S2, so the claim of fewer integrals must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's main claimed saving in the number of double integrals is invalid, and its comparison with Algorithms alg1 and alg2 is unsupported.
issues.title: Appendix algorithm integral count is false
issues.why_classification: The false count removes the appendix algorithm's advertised advantage, but the main paper's algorithms are unaffected.
